newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock exchange trading turnover hits record.
newsitem.headline: China stock exchange trading turnover hits record.

text.p: Turnover on China's two stock exchanges hit a record high of 3.075 trillion yuan in the first half of this year, up 276 percent year-on-year, the Shanghai Securities News said on Sunday.
The Shanghai bourse traded 1.861 trillion yuan, up 209 percent against the same 1996 period and the Shenzhen exchange traded 1.214 trillion yuan, up 465 percent, the newspaper said.
One of the main reasons for the surge in turnover was a large number of new share issues, the newspaper said.
The Shanghai stock exchange listed 59 new firms, including three foreign currency B share firms, with a combined total of 14.8 billion new shares in the first half of the year.
The Shenzhen stock exchange listed 90 firms in the same period, including five B share firms, for a total of 20 billion new shares, the newspaper said.
By the end of June, Shanghai had a total of 388 listed companies with 81.9 billion shares with a market capitalisation of 861.3 billion yuan.
Shenzhen had 360 listed firms at end-June with a total of 64 billion shares on a market capitalisation of 805.2 billion yuan.
Both of China's stock exchanges were established in 1990.
